title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study (verifier‑consistency under identical inputs)
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that tested a single preregistered estimand: verifier‑consistency under identical inputs (i.e., whether a deterministic validator produces different pass/fail outcomes when presented with the same canonical candidate under two scoring conditions). Using template‑synthesized intent→config tasks (N=120) and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), we generated one canonical LLM candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate) and reused it for both conditions. Results: baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, shared seed_0) = 120/120 verifier passes; paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00,0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Model_call accounting: a single canonical generation per task was produced (model_calls_used = 120; maximum_model_calls = 240). We publish exhaustive artifacts (responses, provider traces, per‑episode validator JSON traces, and an execution manifest with SHA‑256 fingerprints) enabling byte‑for‑byte reruns. Importantly, because the preregistered estimand used identical inputs per pair, the confirmatory outcome does not estimate independent generative reliability. We (i) document the artifact‑visible causal chain that produced the degenerate paired contingency (identical canonical candidates + deterministic validator), and (ii) provide artifact‑grounded runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory designs, validator diversification, and task heterogeneity expansions) that preserve reproducibility while answering the operational question practitioners typically require (independent per‑condition pass probability). The immutable initial master prompt is archived (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent into device configuration is safety‑critical in NetOps: misordered or incorrect commands can break reachability, violate ACL intent, or cause unsafe transients. Deterministic offline validators (reachability/ACL/routing analyzers) are standard pre‑deployment oracles for semantic correctness [Batfish lineage; Brown et al., 2023]. LLMs enable fluent intent→config generation but introduce stochasticity and failure modes. We preregistered (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1) a narrow, explicit estimand: verifier‑consistency under identical inputs (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) and a confirmatory paired design over N = 120 synthetic tasks. The purpose was to (a) execute the frozen plan end‑to‑end with exhaustive artifact logging, (b) transparently report the confirmatory inference that follows from the archived artifacts, and (c) diagnose design‑visible reasons why the paired contrast may be uninformative about independent generative reliability and propose artifact‑grounded reruns that answer that operational question.
sections.related_work: Prior verifier‑grounded NetOps work couples generation with deterministic validation and often adopts generate–validate–repair loops. Methodological axes that materially affect measured reliability are: sampling semantics (shared canonical candidate vs. independent per‑condition sampling), repair budget (single‑pass vs. bounded iterative repair), and validator scope (syntactic vs. semantic reachability/ACL/routing checks). Independent sampling and multi‑seed designs estimate generative reliability directly; shared‑candidate designs test validator determinism or scoring reproducibility. We follow and extend this literature by publishing exhaustive artifacts (responses, provider traces, scoring traces) so readers can deterministically replay either paradigm.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The study preregistration (artifact SHA‑256 7db1663c...) defined: N=120 paired tasks (40 per topology class), model = declared gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...), deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0), primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one canonical LLM candidate per task reused for both conditions), analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 with bootstrap (10k resamples, seed = 1729). Task synthesis. Tasks are programmatic templates encoding initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit required_sequence, and workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups). Representative task manifests and shared canonical responses are archived (e.g., execution/task_manifest.jsonl; execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be...). Generation and accounting. The pipeline produced one canonical generation per task (shared_initial), reused for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes; hence model_calls_used = 120 while planned maximum_model_calls = 240. Provider traces and call_cache entries are archived under execution/provider_calls/* and execution/call_cache/*. Deterministic scoring and archived traces. The validator enforces transient workflow_policies and final_state invariants and emits per‑episode JSON scoring traces archived under execution/scoring/*.json (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...). Analysis. We executed the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1: computed paired contingency, bootstrap CI (10k resamples seed=1729), and exact McNemar two‑sided test. All analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...).
sections.results: Confirmatory counts (artifact‑grounded). All confirmatory episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0). Counts: baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count = 120/120. Paired contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...). Primary estimand and inference (preregistered): paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Representative validator traces: each scored episode includes parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, transient‑constraint enforcement, and final_state (see execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad... and execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 8f38c8be...). Model call accounting: model_calls_used = 120 because a single canonical generation per task was produced and reused for both conditions—this accounting is visible in execution/provider_calls/* and execution/responses/* files; full manifest with file SHA‑256s is in execution/execution_manifest.json.
sections.discussion: What the confirmatory result legitimately shows. The preregistered confirmatory estimand tested validator consistency under identical inputs; the archived artifacts show identical canonical candidates per pair and deterministic validator scoring, so identical pass/fail outputs are the expected and correct result. What it does not show. It does not estimate independent generative reliability (the probability that independently sampled LLM candidates satisfy the validator). That operational question requires independent_per_condition sampling or multi‑seed replication, which were not executed under the confirmatory semantics recorded here. Artifact‑grounded runnable modifications. The published bundle permits deterministic reruns implementing informative designs: (A) independent_per_condition rerun — generate separate seeds per condition per task (baseline seed_i, guarded seed_j) and rescore with the archived validator; (B) multi‑seed confirmatory design — generate K≥3 independent seeds per condition per task and estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (C) validator diversification — add an orthogonal verifier and report intersection/union pass rates. Exact artifact paths required to perform these reruns deterministically are included: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e2...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/responses/*, execution/provider_calls/*, execution/scoring/*.json, execution/execution_manifest.json. Threats to validity (artifact‑visible). Internal: shared_initial design removes generation variance. Construct: template‑tight tasks and single validator can overstate performance relative to open natural language intents. External: single declared model and synthetic tasks limit generalization. Contamination: preregistered string overlap heuristics flagged no confirmatory items, but such heuristics cannot definitively rule out pretraining exposure. Reproducibility stance. We publish exhaustive per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints (execution/execution_manifest.json) so third parties can perform byte‑for‑byte reruns and execute the alternate, informative experimental designs without altering the original archived artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired test that answered the preregistered estimand—verifier‑consistency under identical inputs—and published the complete artifact bundle permitting exact reruns. The degenerate paired contingency (both conditions 120/120 passes) is an artifact‑visible consequence of two frozen design choices: (1) generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one canonical LLM candidate generated per task and reused for both conditions), and (2) template‑tight tasks whose required_sequences satisfy canonical candidates. Because the confirmatory estimand differs from the operational quantity practitioners usually require (independent per‑condition generative reliability), we provide artifact‑grounded runnable modifications (independent_per_condition, multi‑seed, validator diversification) and exact paths/SHA‑256 fingerprints so others may deterministically execute those follow‑ups while preserving reproducibility. All execution and analysis artifacts—preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663c..., initial master prompt provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 1872df1e..., model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2..., and per‑episode scoring traces (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...)—are included in the submission bundle for independent audit.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
